subject: English
passage: Maria Montessori developed her educational methods between 1900 and 1930. She believed children should learn through hands-on exploration of their environment. She encouraged students in her schools to move freely around the classroom and choose their own activities. Montessori even designed special child-sized furniture to give students independence. At the time, traditional education emphasized strict discipline, so students were expected to sit quietly in rows and follow rigid schedules. As a result, children typically remained seated and silent for most of the school day. The approach to learning in Montessori's schools was therefore ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: adopted by many of Montessori's contemporaries.
choices.B: familiar to students who had attended other schools.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer. The text tells us that students 'typically remained seated and silent for most of the school day' in traditional schools from 1900 to 1930. This suggests that the hands-on, movement-based approach in Montessori's schools was very unusual for the time.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. The text never discusses educational methods today, so there's no basis for this inference.
